title: A chemical foundation model guides high-conductivity electrolyte formulation
summary: Researchers fine-tuned the SMI-TED chemical foundation model on 13,666 literature measurements of ionic conductivity and screened 100,000 generated electrolyte formulations. Sixteen selected formulations were measured experimentally, with seven exceeding 10 mS/cm. A model-generated LiFSI formulation measured 19.14 mS/cm at room temperature, 82% above the best literature value in the paper’s comparison; the model had predicted 10.52 mS/cm. Conductivity is only one electrolyte property and does not establish electrochemical stability, safety or battery performance. The article was published 2025-08-30; a later correction changed an author name only.
ai_technology: SMI-TED chemical foundation model fine-tuned for electrolyte mixture ionic-conductivity prediction and generative screening

evidence.tested: Sixteen selected formulations were measured by triplicate EIS at 20 °C; seven exceeded 10 mS/cm. A generated LiFSI electrolyte measured 19.14 mS/cm, compared with a model prediction of 10.52 mS/cm and 82% higher conductivity than the best literature value used in the paper comparison.
evidence.unknown: High ionic conductivity alone does not establish electrochemical stability, compatibility with particular electrodes, safety, cycle life or commercial battery performance.
evidence.ai_role: SMI-TED was fine-tuned on literature ionic-conductivity data and screened 100,000 generated formulations; selected candidates were prepared and measured experimentally.

source_review.scope: Primary publisher full text including methods, measured outcomes, affiliations and publication date; primary publisher correction.
